scenario.summary: Threat actors use Microsoft Teams to impersonate help desk staff and persuade users to grant remote access via Quick Assist. From this foothold, they execute scripts via portable runtimes to discover and abuse AD CS configurations, specifically ESC1 and ESC8, to escalate privileges and obtain persistent domain access.

meta.rationale: Prioritize identifying any host that ran Quick Assist in the last 14 days. Filter on users who have not recently opened official support tickets.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder has impersonated help desk staff via Microsoft Teams to establish a remote support session and execute portable runtimes from a user-writable directory to begin system discovery.

hunt.name: Teams Impersonation and Portable Runtime Execution
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the transition from external social engineering to hands-on-keyboard access. It follows a phased approach: first, it identifies hosts with recent Quick Assist activity or cross-tenant Teams authentications. Second, it pivots to those hosts to find portable runtimes (Python, Bun, or Java) launched from user-profile staging directories that then execute system discovery commands. This behavior-based approach detects the execution environment and session context rather than relying solely on file indicators.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, user_name, MIN(time) AS first_seen, MAX(time) AS last_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\quickassist.exe' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, user_name
config.description: Identify hosts that have recently run Quick Assist, the primary vector for hands-on-keyboard access in this campaign.
config.expected_signal: Hosts where Quick Assist was launched. None means no Quick Assist sessions occurred on managed hosts in this window.

primitive_config.label: Scope hosts using Quick Assist
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, user_name, MIN(time) AS first_seen, MAX(time) AS last_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\quickassist.exe' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, user_name
primitive_config.expected: Hosts where Quick Assist was launched. None means no Quick Assist sessions occurred on managed hosts in this window.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, actor_user_name, home_tenant_id, resource_tenant_id, time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE provider = 'm365' AND home_tenant_id != resource_tenant_id AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find users authenticating via Teams where the home tenant does not match the resource tenant, indicating cross-tenant contact.
config.expected_signal: A sign-in from an external tenant. This identifies the social engineering contact point.

primitive_config.label: Teams authentication from external tenants
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, actor_user_name, home_tenant_id, resource_tenant_id, time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE provider = 'm365' AND home_tenant_id != resource_tenant_id AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A sign-in from an external tenant. This identifies the social engineering contact point.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, file_name, actor_user_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE activity_id = 1 AND LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\users\\%' AND LOWER(file_name) LIKE LOWER('{{staging_pattern}}') AND file_type = 'directory' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find the creation of the specific staging directories used to host portable runtimes under user profiles.
config.expected_signal: New folders created under a user profile matching the staging prefix. None means no such folders were detected.

primitive_config.label: KB-prefixed staging directory creation

primitive_config.expected: New folders created under a user profile matching the staging prefix. None means no such folders were detected.

config.objective: Identify hosts where a remote session was established followed by suspicious file staging or external authentication. Provide a list of hostnames to focus the next behaviour search.
config.description: Determine if the Quick Assist usage, external Teams auth, and staging activity suggest a successful impersonation attempt.
config.expected_signal: Identification of hosts with evidence of social engineering and staging.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict of suspicious or benign, citing specific events.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, process_original_file_name, process_hash_sha256, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\\users\\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\\appdata\\%') AND (instr(',' || '{{discovery_commands}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_original_file_name) || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{runtime_hashes}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_hash_sha256) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify discovery commands that processes in staging directories launch.
config.expected_signal: System discovery processes like ipconfig or tasklist running from a portable runtime located in a user profile.

config.instructions: Isolate the host and revoke any active Teams sessions for the user. Collect the binary and scripts found in the KB-prefixed directory for analysis.

config.instructions: Examine the file creation events in the identified KB-prefixed directory. Verify if scripts were executed. Pivot to hb_network_connection to see if LDAPS or SMB connections were made to domain controllers.
